Shri Anokhi Lal Kharol, learned counsel for the Objecto  ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

M.Cr.C. Nos.26621/2024 & 25041/2024 are first bail applications and M.Cr.C. No.29060/2024 is repeat second bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (now section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) for grant of bail to the applicants, in connection with FIR/Crime No.873/2023, Date:-(Not mentioned) registered at P.S.-Industrial Area, Jaora, District- Ratlam (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 201,
120-B of the IPC.
2. First bail application of applicant-Makhan Singh was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 24.04.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.14208/2024.

3. Prosecution story in brief is that the applicants/ accused persons entered into criminal conspiracy with intent to cheat the complainant Pradeep and in furtherance of the conspiracy the accused persons induced the complainant Pradeep to purchase a land for investment and told him that thereby he will gain a good profit.

The accused persons received a sum of Rs.94,00,000/- during period 01/03/2022-23/12/2023 in different installments from complainant through cash, R.T.G.S.
and online payment.

To convince the complainant, the accused persons showed him an agreement to sell of land dated 16.03.2022 bearing survey number 246/12 area of 0.5060 Hectare situated at village Ringnod tehsil Jawra, distt.- Ratlam, wherein the seller was Shakir Hussain and buyers were accused Mukesh NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23427 3 MCRC-26621-2024 Choudhary, complainant Pradeep and Jagdeesh which was executed in the absence of the complainant Pradeep.
There was no signature of complainant Pradeep in the agreement.
During investigation, it was revealed that the aforesaid agreement was forged.
Later on the accused persons could not get the aforesaid land registered in complainant's name, then the complainant asked the accused persons to return his money.

Complainant told the accused persons that he will get them implicated in a criminal case then accused Mukesh Choudhary had given him a cheque of Rs.70,00,000/- and said that if he could not get the land transferred the complainant can withdraw the amount.

After some time when the land could not be registered then the complainant said that he will lodge a report, then accused Mukesh Choudhary gave 3 cheques of Indusland Bank account of Mukesh Gouri having a sum of Rs.94,00,000/- to the complainant but when the complainant inquired in the bank, he came to know that only Rs.14/- is left in the bank account of Mukesh Gouri.
When this fact was told to accused Mukesh Choudhary, he asked the complainant to return the aforesaid cheque and he gave a cheque of ICICI Bank account of Mubarik having a sum of Rs.94,00,000/-.
The complainant said that once the cheque of Mubarik gets cleared, he will return the previous cheques given to him by accused Mukesh.
Upon presentation, the complainant came to know that bank balance of Mubarik is nil.

Aforesaid cheques were recovered and seized from the Kalim Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128707768/

Rs.1,10,000/- and a blur picture affixed in the place of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23427 4 MCRC-26621-2024
Shakir's picture in forged agreement was recovered from accused Kalim.
4. Learned counsels for the applicants/ accused persons submits that, the applicants have not committed the offence and have falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that name of the applicant/ accused Kalim Khan is not mentioned in the written complaint filed by the complainant as well as in the FIR.
It is also submitted that the applicant is implicated in the case merely on the basis of memorandum statement given by co-accused.

As per report of handwriting expert,
signatures of the applicant are not matching with the signature of the alleged forged agreement to sell.
Learned counsel for the applicant Makhan Singh submitted that the applicant has nothing to do with the said deal taken place between the complainant and accused Mukesh Choudhary.
It is submitted that the applicant Makhan Singh received Rs.10,00,000/- from complainant which was against the payment of money borrowed by the complainant.
It is also submitted that the applicant was just a witness of the alleged agreement.
Learned counsel for the applicant Mukesh also submitted that there is no legal evidence available against him in the case.
From the statement of the witnesses recorded u/S 161 of Cr.P.C., no case is made out against him.
Learned counsels for the applicants also submitted that applicants Mukesh Choudhary and Makhan Singh are in custody since 03/03/2024 and applicant Kalim Khan is in custody since 29/04/2024.
after dismissal of first bail application of Makhan Singh as was withdrawn, chargesheet has been filed.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicants be released on bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23427 5 MCRC-26621-2024 5.

On other hand learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the Objector have opposed the prayer and submitted that the accused persons have made a forged agreement to sell dated 16/03/2022 while Shakir Hussain in his statement recorded u/S 161 of Cr.P.C. clearly stated that he did not execute the aforesaid agreement.
His statement is also supported by handwriting expert's report.
The accused persons have also used the aforesaid agreement and cheated the complainant and wrongfully gained a sum of Rs.94,00,000/-.
The offence is serious in nature.
The accused persons are an influenced persons so they can influence the witnesses, there is also possibility of them absconding.
Applicant Kaleem Khan has 2 criminal antecedents.
Therefore, the applicants are not entitled for bail.

6. Having heard learned counsels for the parties, perused the case- diary also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in view of this court, the possibility of threat and inducement to witnesses and tempering of evidence cannot be denied.
Also considering the increase in the number of these types of offences in all the developing regions, this court is of considered opinion that it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicants.
Resultantly, applications for bail are rejected.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ajit Kalim Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128707768/
